title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The one cache a checkout did not drop
summary: A file changing on disk evicts six caches. The workspace corpus was not one of them, so a checkout left it serving offsets from the old content for a minute.

highlights.title: A checkout fires no save event
highlights.description: The corpus was dropped on save, and a git checkout or a stash pop touches files nobody has open. Its offsets stayed measured on content that was gone.

highlights.title: The burst path is the checkout path
highlights.description: The watcher has a separate path for the hundreds of files a checkout changes at once. That is exactly the one that mattered, and it drops the corpus too.

highlights.title: Both entry points
highlights.description: The desktop and the browser builds share this wiring. Fixing one and leaving the other is how a change ships half applied.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A file changed on disk drops the workspace corpus, on the per file path and on the burst path.
The browser entry point gets the same eviction as the desktop one.
